element.name: Market Agility & Competitive Pressure
element.documentation: In an AI-driven landscape the "cost of delay" is existential. If the bank cannot deliver features as fast as a startup or a tech giant, it loses market share.

element.name: Regulatory Resiliency & Social License
element.documentation: For a major financial institution, non-compliance with APRA CPS 230/234 is a threat to the banking license. Manual compliance is too slow and error-prone for an AI-speed world.

element.name: Systemic Sustainability & Complexity Management
element.documentation: Unmanaged architectural drift creates hidden debt that makes systems fragile. Left unchecked, the system eventually becomes too complex to change at any speed.

element.name: Human-to-Machine Operational Scaling
element.documentation: Human architects are a finite bottleneck. As AI agents produce changes at machine speed, it is physically impossible to review it all with traditional methods.

element.name: Architecture as Executable Intelligence
element.documentation: Transform architecture from passive documentation into executable system intelligence.

element.name: Deterministic Human Accountability
element.documentation: AI is advisory; the specification is deterministic; a human holds sign-off.

element.name: Forensic Auditability
element.documentation: Ability to reconstruct not just what happened but why a decision was made.

element.name: Policy as Code
element.documentation: All governance rules, compliance mappings, and architectural guardrails are expressed as version-controlled, machine-executable policy, not prose documents.

element.name: APRA CPS 230/234 Compliance
element.documentation: Operational resilience and prudential standards.

element.name: Model Risk Management Framework
element.documentation: Manages risks associated with models and agentic decision-making.

element.name: Australian Privacy Act (APP)
element.documentation: Data privacy and protection regulations.

element.name: Cloud & Data Sovereignty Policy
element.documentation: Governance and compliance policies for cloud-based operations.

element.name: Model Risk Standards (SR 11-7 / APRA)
element.documentation: External standards governing model risk management. SR 11-7 is the de facto global standard adopted by major banks; APRA's operational resilience guidance sets the Australian prudential expectation. Together they define validation, documentation, and oversight obligations for agentic decision-making.

element.name: Automated Specification Generation from Graph
element.documentation: For every approved change request, the system must automatically derive a complete, executable architectural specification from the knowledge graph — with zero manual authoring by an architect.

element.name: Automated Regulatory Obligation Mapping
element.documentation: Every technical change must be automatically mapped to its applicable APRA CPS 230/234 obligations before a deployment gate is passed. No change may proceed without a resolved compliance mapping.

element.name: Pre-Deployment Compliance Gate Enforcement
element.documentation: The supervisory control plane must intercept and evaluate all agent-generated changes against the executable specification before they reach any test or production environment. Non-compliant changes must be blocked, not flagged retrospectively.

element.name: Continuous As-Built vs. As-Designed Reconciliation
element.documentation: The system must continuously reconcile observed system state (telemetry, deployed artefacts) against the knowledge graph's as-designed intent and surface any deviation as a classified drift event.

element.name: Mandatory Human Sign-off for Non-Standard Changes
element.documentation: Any change that cannot be deterministically validated against the executable specification must be escalated to a named human architect for explicit approval. The system must prevent autonomous resolution of ambiguous compliance cases.

element.name: Digital Twin Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: Maintain a live, queryable graph of the enterprise technology landscape — its components, policies, relationships, and regulatory mappings — as the authoritative source of architectural truth.

element.name: Executable Specification Generation
element.documentation: Deterministically produce machine-consumable architectural specifications from the knowledge graph, which AI agents and CI/CD pipelines consume as guardrails rather than human-readable documents.

element.name: Agentic Supervisory Control
element.documentation: Constrain, monitor, and intervene in the behaviour of autonomous development agents in real time, enforcing architectural and regulatory boundaries before code reaches any environment.

element.name: Forensic Audit & Compliance Ledger
element.documentation: Record every agent action, gate decision, and specification evaluation into an immutable, queryable ledger that serves as contemporaneous evidence for regulatory examination.

element.name: Architectural Drift Detection & Reconciliation
element.documentation: Continuously compare observed system telemetry against the as-designed knowledge graph and surface deviations — strategic, structural, or agentic — in real time.

element.name: Human Oversight & Approval Workflow
element.documentation: Identify, route, and manage human architect approval for changes that deviate from deterministic specifications or present ambiguous compliance scenarios, through a defined, auditable sign-off process that upholds principle-human-accountability.

element.name: Deterministic Spec Generation
element.documentation: Scripted, template-driven generation of executable architectural specifications from the knowledge graph. AI recommends scope; human holds sign-off. Output is the deterministic intent consumed by the agentic crew.

element.name: Agentic Development Execution
element.documentation: Supervised execution of AI-driven development within supervisory control plane constraints. Consumes the executable specification, regulation, policy, patterns, and controls from the knowledge graph to generate code, test suites, and deployment manifests.

element.name: Automated CICD Gate Execution
element.documentation: The CI/CD pipeline with the agentic control plane woven in. Evaluates every artefact against the executable specification and policy-as-code gates before a release is permitted. Blocks on violation; escalates exceptions for human review; logs all gate outcomes to the immutable ledger.

element.name: Production Release
element.documentation: Compliant, traceable-to-spec deployment to production, triggered only after all gates have cleared. Automatically auditable end-to-end.

element.name: Current State Discovery
element.documentation: Continuous, automated reconciliation of actual system state against architectural intent. Surfaces classified drift events for human review; does not write directly to the backlog.

element.name: Drift Review & Triage Gate
element.documentation: Human-gated review of drift findings before they are committed as backlog work items. A Solution Architect approves architectural drift; Security & Compliance approves regulatory drift. Ensures only validated, prioritised findings enter the delivery pipeline.

element.name: Frictionless Architecture Platform
element.documentation: Governs architecture from authored policy through to BAU control effectiveness.

element.name: Controls & Compliance Catalog
element.documentation: Authors custom policies and standards and converts them to OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles.

property.value: Policy & Standards Authoring Workspace (Trestle Markdown catalogs); Trestle Conversion Service (Markdown <-> OSCAL Catalogs & Profiles).

element.name: Reusable Architecture Library
element.documentation: Composable patterns, blueprints and solution designs with OSCAL references, plus threat modelling.

property.value: Architecture Pattern Library (technology-agnostic; -> OSCAL Profiles); Implementation Blueprint Library (parent/child of patterns; -> OSCAL Components); Solution Design Composer (SolutionComponents under a SolutionDesign; -> OSCAL SSP); Threat Modelling Service (attaches threats & mitigations).

element.name: Digital Twin & Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: Maintains the Architecture Knowledge Graph: an intent plane and a current-state digital twin plane.

property.value: Digital Twin Ingestion Service (builds the current-state plane from live infra & pipeline data).

element.name: Architecture Governance
element.documentation: Models candidate future-state / solution options, evaluates them, decides, and archives the rest with reasons.

property.value: Future-State & Options Modeller (one or more candidate architectures, e.g. RFP vendor responses); Architecture Governance Service (comparative evaluation, impact assessment, ADR decisions, archival of rejected options with rationale).

element.name: Conformance & Drift Assurance
element.documentation: Enforces controls at release, monitors effectiveness in BAU, and detects and reports architecture drift.

property.value: Controls Enforcement Gate (release-time); Controls Effectiveness Monitor (BAU); Drift & Deviation Engine (intent vs twin); Architecture Drift Dashboard & Backlog.

element.name: Modelling & Specification
element.documentation: Out-of-the-box ArchiMate / C4 / UML modelling, and generation of development specifications.

property.value: Modelling & Notation Engine (ArchiMate, C4, UML); Specification Generator (specs from patterns, blueprints & designs for spec-driven development).

element.name: OSCAL Repository
element.documentation: OSCAL Catalogs, Profiles, Components and SSPs.

element.name: Pattern & Blueprint Repository
element.documentation: Architecture patterns, implementation blueprints and solution designs.

element.name: Architecture Knowledge Graph
element.documentation: One graph store, two planes: Architecture Intent and Current-State Digital Twin.

element.name: Framework Pack Library
element.documentation: NIST / FedRAMP baselines; ArchiMate / C4 / UML metamodels.

element.name: Enterprise Architect
element.documentation: Owns principles, target patterns, options and governance decisions.

element.name: Solution Architect
element.documentation: Composes blueprints into solution designs.

element.name: Security Architect / Threat Modeller
element.documentation: Runs threat models over patterns, blueprints and designs.

element.name: Developer
element.documentation: Consumes generated specifications for delivery.

element.name: Compliance Officer / Auditor
element.documentation: Authors control content and verifies traceability.

element.name: Platform Operations (BAU)
element.documentation: Watches control effectiveness and drift in run.

element.name: Source Control
element.documentation: Git repositories for specifications and delivery code.

element.name: CI/CD Pipeline
element.documentation: Builds, tests and releases; invokes the enforcement gate.

element.name: Cloud & Infrastructure Platforms
element.documentation: Runtime platforms whose live state feeds the digital twin.

element.name: IT Service Management / Backlog
element.documentation: Delivery backlog and ticketing (e.g. Jira).

element.name: Regulatory Content Sources
element.documentation: Upstream NIST OSCAL content and FedRAMP baselines.

element.name: LLM Provider
element.documentation: Language model used for drafting specs, ADRs, evaluations and threat narratives.

element.name: RFP / Vendor Submissions
element.documentation: Requests for proposal and competing vendor solution responses assessed at engagement time.

element.name: Policy & Standards Authoring

element.documentation: Convert authored Markdown and upstream baselines into OSCAL Catalogs and Profiles (Trestle round-trip).

element.name: Solution Design Composition

element.name: Threat Modelling

element.name: Future-State & Options Modelling

element.name: Comparative Evaluation & Decision
element.documentation: Compare candidate options, assess impact against intent and twin, record the ADR, and archive rejected options with rationale.

element.name: Controls Enforcement Gate

element.name: Controls Effectiveness Monitoring
